title: Explicit ring-square maps and naturality of polynomial bar comparisons
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ as in [def-weil-size-convention], and a commutative square of $\mathcal U$-small commutative rings $(\alpha:A\to A',\beta:B\to B')$ from $A\to B$ to $A'\to B'$. Write $P_n=(F_AU)^{n+1}B$ and $P'_n=(F_{A'}U)^{n+1}B'$, with evaluation faces, unit degeneracies and iterated evaluation augmentations, where $F_A(E)=A[E]$. Define $t_{-1}=\beta$ and recursively $t_n:P_n=A[UP_{n-1}]\to A'[UP'_{n-1}]=P'_n$ by sending $a$ to $\alpha(a)$ and $[p]$ to $[t_{n-1}(p)]$ for $n\geq0$. These are semilinear augmented simplicial maps. They preserve identity squares and composition strictly. Let $\mathcal D_{B/A}$ and $\mathcal D_{B'/A'}$ be the categories of all $\mathcal U$-small polynomial algebras augmented to the respective targets, with algebra maps over those targets. Put $\mathcal F_{B/A}(T)=\Omega^1_{T/A}\otimes_T B$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], with maps $\mathrm dx\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm d(vx)\otimes b$ for $v:T\to T'$, and define $\mathcal F_{B'/A'}$ similarly. The square induces the functor
$$u(T)=(T\otimes_A A'\to B'),\qquad x\otimes a'\mapsto\beta(\epsilon_T(x))a',$$
and the natural transformation $\theta:\mathcal F_{B/A}\to\operatorname{Res}_\beta(\mathcal F_{B'/A'}\circ u)$ with formula $\mathrm dx\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm d(x\otimes1)\otimes\beta(b)$; $A[E]\otimes_A A'\cong A'[E]$. For augmented simplicial $\mathcal U$-small polynomial algebras $Q\to B$ and $Q'\to B'$ (so every $Q_n$ is an object of $\mathcal D_{B/A}$ and every $Q'_n$ one of $\mathcal D_{B'/A'}$) whose underlying augmentations are trivial Kan fibrations [def-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-fibration], and any augmented $\alpha$-semilinear simplicial map $h:Q\to Q'$, there is a simplicial map $k:uQ\to Q'$ given by $q\otimes a'\mapsto h(q)a'$. Put $K(Q)=s(\mathcal F_{B/A}(Q))$, where $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$ with alternating-face differential and zero positive terms. The rule $\mathrm dq\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm d(hq)\otimes\beta(b)$ gives a chain map $K(h):K(Q)\to\operatorname{Res}_\beta K(Q')$; for standard $h=t$ these maps preserve identities and composition strictly. In $D(B)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] the canonical bar comparisons of [lem-trf-polynomial-presentation-homology] satisfy
$$a_{Q'}K(h)=\mathbf H(u,\theta)a_Q.$$
Here $\mathbf H(u,\theta)$ sends the bar generator $(T_0\to\cdots\to T_n,x)$ to $(uT_0\to\cdots\to uT_n,\theta_{T_0}(x))$ and restriction of scalars along $\beta$ is understood on all target objects. This formula applies to $h=t$ for standard resolutions. No assumption that $uQ\to B'$ is a resolution and no flatness or injectivity hypothesis on $\alpha$ or $\beta$ is required.

proof.text: Put $P_{-1}=B$ and $P'_{-1}=B'$. Given $t_{n-1}$, substitution in finite polynomials defines the unique ring map $t_n:A[UP_{n-1}]\to A'[UP'_{n-1}]$ taking coefficients through $\alpha$ and $[p]$ to $[t_{n-1}(p)]$. It is $\alpha$-semilinear by its value on coefficients. Starting with the ring map $t_{-1}=\beta$ therefore constructs every $t_n$. Uniqueness follows because coefficients and variables generate the polynomial ring; this applies without a finite variable set.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), explicit standard polynomial maps and presentation-category base change.

proof.text: For a semilinear algebra map $f:X\to X'$, write $L(f):A[UX]\to A'[UX']$ for this substitution. Evaluation satisfies $\epsilon' L(f)=f\epsilon$: on $[x]$ both sides are $f(x)$, and on coefficients this is semilinearity. The unit-induced map $\delta:A[UX]\to A[U(A[UX])]$ sends $[x]$ to $[[x]]$ and coefficients to coefficients. Thus $\delta' L(f)=L(L(f))\delta$, on $[x]$ by the common value $[[f(x)]]$, and on coefficients by $\alpha$. Apply these identities at each nested polynomial level of the faces and degeneracies specified in [lem-trf-polynomial-augmentation-boundary]. They give $d'_it_n=t_{n-1}d_i$ and $s'_it_n=t_{n+1}s_i$; iterating evaluation gives augmentation compatibility, with degree $-1$ equal to the original ring square. Finally $L(1)=1$ and $L(gf)=L(g)L(f)$ on coefficients and variables. Induction starting at $t_{-1}$ proves the strict identity and composition laws for all $t_n$.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), explicit standard polynomial maps and presentation-category base change.

proof.text: For an object $T\xrightarrow{\epsilon_T}B$, the rule $x\otimes a'\mapsto\beta(\epsilon_T(x))a'$ is balanced over $A$, since $\beta\epsilon_T(a)=\alpha(a)$ in $B'$. It is an $A'$-algebra augmentation. For an arrow $v:T\to S$ use $u(v)(x\otimes a')=v(x)\otimes a'$; augmentation compatibility and the identity and composition equations follow on pure tensors. If $T=A[E]$, define $T\otimes_A A'\to A'[E]$ by $p\otimes a'\mapsto a'\alpha_*(p)$ and its inverse by $a'\mapsto1\otimes a'$ and $e\mapsto e\otimes1$. On coefficients, variables and pure tensors the composites are identities. Hence $u(T)$ is polynomial. Finite-support polynomial expressions and the tensor quotient are $\mathcal U$-small, so $u$ really lands in the stated presentation category, including when $E$ is empty or infinite.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), explicit standard polynomial maps and presentation-category base change.

proof.text: The differential presentation in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] verifies all coefficient maps directly. For $v:T\to S$ over $B$, $\mathrm dx\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm d(vx)\otimes b$ preserves additivity and the Leibniz relation, and kills $\mathrm da$ for $a\in A$; tensor balancing holds because $\epsilon_Sv=\epsilon_T$. These maps are functorial on the generators. For $\theta_T$, use the same relations with $x\mapsto x\otimes1$ and $b\mapsto\beta(b)$. Constants from $A$ land in $A'$, so their relative differentials vanish. A scalar $t\in T$ acts on the target tensor as $\beta\epsilon_T(t)$, exactly the image under $\beta$ of its action on the source tensor; this proves the balancing and $B$-linearity after restriction. For $v:T\to S$, the two naturality composites both send $\mathrm dx\otimes b$ to $\mathrm d(v(x)\otimes1)\otimes\beta(b)$, proving that $\theta$ is a natural transformation.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), explicit standard polynomial maps and presentation-category base change.

proof.text: The formula $k_n(q\otimes a')=h_n(q)a'$ is balanced because $h_n(aq)=\alpha(a)h_n(q)$, is an $A'$-algebra map, and respects augmentation because $\epsilon' h_n=\beta\epsilon$. Each simplicial operator is an $A'$-algebra map on the target, so its commutation with $k$ follows on $q\otimes a'$ from its commutation with $h$. Thus $k:uQ\to Q'$ is simplicial. Applying the differential relations of [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives degreewise maps $\mathrm dq\otimes b\mapsto\mathrm d(h_nq)\otimes\beta(b)$. For each face, the two composites agree since $d'_i h_n=h_{n-1}d_i$; their alternating sums therefore commute as well. This constructs $K(h)$. For $h=t$, its identity and composition equations follow from Step 2 on every $\mathrm dq\otimes b$, which generates the module.

source.place: Tag 08QL (section-functoriality), explicit standard polynomial maps and presentation-category base change.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-presentation-homology] separately to $Q$ over $B/A$ and $Q'$ over $B'/A'$, using $R=B,F=\mathcal F_{B/A}$ and $R'=B',F'=\mathcal F_{B'/A'}$. It supplies small presentation categories, representable contractibility for both resolutions, and their canonical comparisons with the first-vertex bar model. Consequently [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation] applies with these two categories, $\rho=\beta$, and $u,\theta,k$ from Steps 3--5. Its comparison maps are the $a_Q,a_{Q'}$ just specified: the presentation-homology statement explicitly uses that canonical bar comparison. On generators, $F'(k_n)\theta_{Q_n}(\mathrm dq\otimes b)=\mathrm d(k_n(q\otimes1))\otimes\beta(b)=\mathrm d(h_nq)\otimes\beta(b)$, so its map $s(F'(k)\theta_Q)$ is precisely $K(h)$. Its stated naturality equality is therefore $a_{Q'}K(h)=\mathbf H(u,\theta)a_Q$ in $D(B)$. Its bar map sends $(T_0\to\cdots\to T_n,x)$ to $(uT_0\to\cdots\to uT_n,\theta_{T_0}(x))$, exactly as required, with degreewise restriction of target scalars.

proof.text: For the standard endpoints, [lem-trf-polynomial-augmentation-boundary] gives termwise polynomial algebras and trivial Kan augmentations for both $P$ and $P'$. Their terms are $\mathcal U$-small by closure under finite-support polynomial formation, so Step 6 applies with $Q=P,Q'=P',h=t$. The general comparison statement [lem-trf-simplicial-derived-colimit-computation] requires contractibility only for the two endpoint resolutions and explicitly requires none for $uQ$. All remaining constructions were substitutions or balanced maps, with no inverses of ring maps and no exactness assertion for tensoring. Thus the argument imposes no flatness or injectivity hypothesis on either vertical map.
